description: Only films whose replacement cost is strictly higher than 20.99 are used. Films costing exactly 20.99 are excluded.

b.request: For films with `replacement_cost` strictly greater than 20.99, calculate by `rating` the average non-NULL `length` and the average non-NULL `rental_rate / replacement_cost`; then return one row containing the unrounded average of those per-rating averages for `length` and for the ratio, in that order.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_rating_length, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_rating_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS rating_averages;
b.raw: For films with `replacement_cost` strictly greater than 20.99, calculate by `rating` the average non-NULL `length` and the average non-NULL `rental_rate / replacement_cost`; then return one row containing the unrounded average of those per-rating averages for `length` and for the ratio, in that order.

c.request: Looking at the costlier films, with the `replacement_cost` threshold set at 20.99, what are the average running time (`length`) and the average ratio of `rental_rate` to `replacement_cost` for each `rating` (ignoring missing values)? Then summarize them as one row: the average of the per-rating lengths and the average of the per-rating ratios, in that order and unrounded. Only films whose replacement cost is strictly higher than 20.99 are used. Films costing exactly 20.99 are excluded.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(per_rating_avg_length) AS avg_of_rating_avg_lengths, AVG(per_rating_avg_ratio) AS avg_of_rating_avg_ratios FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS per_rating_avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS per_rating_avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS per_rating

d.request: Filter films to those with `replacement_cost > 20.99`; for each rating, calculate the average non-null `length` and average non-null `rental_rate / replacement_cost`, then return one row containing the unrounded averages of those per-rating averages, in that order.
d.sql:
SELECT AVG(avg_length), AVG(avg_rate_to_replacement_cost)
FROM (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(length) AS avg_length,
         AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_rate_to_replacement_cost
  FROM film
  WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99
  GROUP BY rating
) AS rating_averages;

a.request: Using only films whose `replacement_cost` is more than 20.99, find for each `rating` the average running time (`length`) and the average ratio of `rental_rate` to `replacement_cost` (ignoring missing values). Then return one row with the average of those per-rating average lengths and the average of those per-rating average ratios, in that order and unrounded.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_length), AVG(avg_ratio) FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS per_rating
